payload.text: Fidelity evidence names an artifact a later reader can OBTAIN or REBUILD, or states plainly that it cannot and why. MEASURED 2026-09-09 by snorkeltoast and verified by vc: the 45h reel is entirely untracked -- 23 files, 15 MB, ZERO under git, and matched by no ignore rule, so it is unadded rather than deliberately excluded, in a parent directory that does carry 3 tracked files. FLOORS.md therefore cites sha256 daaa503ad7db for a build existing on one machine: the hash identifies the artifact precisely and makes it no easier to obtain, and the sha's only function was to let a reader verify. A PROVENANCE LINE THAT CANNOT BE FOLLOWED IS MOST OF A PROVENANCE LINE MISSING. THE 15 MB IS NOT ONE DECISION AND MUST NOT BE PUT TO hv AS ONE, which is vc's measurement: showreel.yaml is 8 KB in 1 file and is the reel's DESCRIPTION; assets/ is 5.7 MB in 16 files and is the source; _out/ is 9.2 MB in 3 files and is DERIVED, regenerable from the other two and never a thing to commit; plus .raster/ at 256 KB of intermediate cache and a 12 KB .DS_Store, both of which want an ignore rule rather than a decision. So the repository question is 5.7 MB of source images, the config costs nothing, and 9.2 MB of the total is an answer nobody should store. AND OBTAINABLE IS NOT THE SAME AS BYTE-REPRODUCIBLE: committing config and assets makes the reel REBUILDABLE, not identical, because the encoder's bytes depend on its version -- which is the same fact that makes WP-02 necessary for the Rust port at all. A rebuild that yields a different sha is not evidence of a defect and not evidence of its absence; only the harness can tell those apart. So the sha identifies, the inputs make it rebuildable, and the harness makes a rebuild gradeable, and provenance is followable only with all three. DISCHARGED, AND NOT BY TRACKING ANYTHING. hv RULED 2026-09-09 that the reel's inputs stay in Dropbox: the reel lives in a Dropbox worktree rather than a git one, its inputs can be arbitrarily large, and Utilz itself is fully tracked, which is what the hoist actually depends on. THIS ROW IS NOT AN ACTION ITEM AND MUST NOT READ AS ONE -- snorkeltoast's point when the ruling landed. The limit is permanent and TRUE: a later reader cannot resolve sha256 daaa503ad7db, and nobody intends to change that. What the row still requires is the honest half -- FLOORS.md states at the point the sha is read what a reader can and cannot do with it, which it does. The three-legged reading holds and is now the whole of it: the sha identifies, the inputs are unobtainable so nothing makes the reel rebuildable by a third party, and the harness is what makes any rebuild gradeable for whoever does hold the inputs.
